==Biography==
Xpecial hails from Temple City, California in the USA. He began his pro gaming career in many different MMOs as well as being involved in the DOTA pro scene, as it died out he moved onto League of Legends. He became well-known in the League of Legends community as the support player for [[Team SoloMid]], part of the original roster that moved into a gaming house in New York. Along with his teammates, he streamed regularly with commentary and created regular [[Xpecial#Vlogs|vlogs]], earning him a large fan base.

In May 4, 2014, it was announced that Xpecial had been benched from TSM, and later that same day he was picked up by [[Team Curse]]. 

On November 24, Xpecial appeared on the show [[Summoning Insight]] and discussed his time on TSM and Curse.<ref>[http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PBOWmFk9lmM 'Summoning Insight' Episode 30, with special guest Xpecial] ''youtube.com''</ref>

===2015 Season===
Prior to the start of the [[Riot League Championship Series/North America/2015 Season/Spring Season|spring LCS split]], Team Curse merged with the Team Liquid organization and rebranded under the name [[Team Liquid]]. After a few swaps between [[Keith]] and [[Piglet]] as their AD carry, the team ended the season with a 9-9 record and qualified for [[Riot League Championship Series/North America/2015 Season/Spring Playoffs|playoffs]] with the sixth seed after defeating [[Team 8]] in a tiebreaker game. In the playoffs, Liquid beat [[Counter Logic Gaming|CLG]] 3-0 in the quarterfinals before falling to [[Cloud9]] 3-2 in the semifinals; in the third-place match, Liquid finally broke the "fourth-place curse" that stopped them from placing higher than fourth place in any event that had persisted since they were Team Curse and took down [[Team Impulse]] 3-2.

Team Liquid finished the [[Riot League Championship Series/North America/2015 Season/Summer Season|summer split round robin]] in first place after winning a tiebreaker match over Counter Logic Gaming - [[LCS Teams Timeline|the first team]] other than TSM or Cloud9 to place first in an NA LCS round robin. However, in the [[Riot League Championship Series/North America/2015 Season/Summer Playoffs|playoffs]], they lost immediately in the semifinals to TSM, making them also the first team to finish first in an NA LCS round robin but not make the playoff finals. A CLG victory over TSM in the playoff finals sent Team Liquid to the [[2015 Season North America Regional Finals|regional finals]] instead of giving them a direct seed to [[2015 Season World Championship|Worlds]] via [[2015 Season/Championship Points|Championship Points]], and in the gauntlet they lost to underdogs Cloud9, ending their post-season abruptly.

===2016 Preseason===
In September 2015, Xpecial released a vlog confirming that he would be leaving Team Liquid.<ref name="xpecialleavevlog">[http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OPZ7FKyJ3A8 TL Update - Xpecial On His Future] ''youtube.com''</ref> His replacement [[Smoothie]] was announced a few weeks later, and shortly after Xpecial became a free agent.<ref name="smoothiejoin">[http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bEoc3ZD2nSw Team Liquid Smoothie Challenge] ''youtube.com''</ref> In his free agency announcement, he stated that he had played briefly with [[Cloud9]]'s [[Cloud9 Challenger|new Challenger team]] but that it hadn't worked out.<ref name="xpecialleavetl">[http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nJrKim_IYL8 Xpecial - Free Agency, C9 Challenger, Future] ''youtube.com''</ref> He later announced that he would not be playing on any LCS team for the [[League Championship Series/North America/2016 Season/Spring Season|next LCS split]] but that he still intended to continue competing.<ref>[http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H7Uy5H4-2JQ Xpecial - Not in LCS, Motivation, Future] ''youtube.com''</ref>

===2016 Season===
After his attempts to join an LCS team for the 2016 season were unsuccessful, Xpecial joined new [[NA Challenger Series/2016 Season/Spring Season|NACS]] team [[Apex Gaming]].<ref name="joinapex">[http://www.twitlonger.com/show/n_1so78if Saintvicious's Twitlonger] ''twitlonger.com''</ref>

Apex won both the regular season of NACS and the [[NA Challenger Series/2016 Season/Spring Playoffs|playoffs]], using both [[Eve]] and [[Shrimp]] actively in the jungle. In the [[League Championship Series/North America/2016 Season/Summer Promotion|promotion tournament]], they were seeded first against the ninth-place [[Team Impulse]], to whom they lost, and then against second place Challenger team [[Team Dragon Knights]], a rematch of the Challenger Series finals. This time, they didn't even drop one game against TDK and qualified successfully for the [[League Championship Series/North America/2016 Season/Summer Season|LCS summer split]].

Apex started out the split strong, with a 2-0 first week including a 2-1 upset of reigning NA LCS champions and [[2016 Mid-Season Invitational|MSI]] alums [[Counter Logic Gaming|CLG]]. Their success, however, was short-lived, and by week 5 they were in 7th place, where they remained for the rest of the season, out of reach of the [[League Championship Series/North America/2016 Season/Summer Playoffs|playoffs]] but also safe from [[League Championship Series/North America/2017 Season/Spring Promotion|relegations]] for the [[League Championship Series/North America/2017 Season/Spring Season|2017 Spring Season]]. In September, both Team Dignitas and Apex were acquired by the '''Philadelphia 76ers''' in September 2016, to play under the Dignitas name.<ref name="76acquire">[http://team-dignitas.net/articles/news/Team-Dignitas/10251/philadelphia-76ers-acquire-merge-and-manage-leading-esports-teams-dignitas-and-apex Philadelphia 76ers acquire, merge and manage leading esports teams Dignitas and Apex] ''team-dignitas.net''</ref>

===2017 Season===
Xpecial remained with the newly rebranded Dignitas for 2017. The team got off to a bad start in the [[NA LCS/2017 Season/Spring Season|spring split]], going 2-6 over the first four weeks. Xpecial was also subbed out for substitute support [[Stunt]] for a few games, until Stunt went to [[Phoenix1]] in March and Xpecial regained his starting spot. The team improved after [[Cop]] was rehired as head coach, going 7-3 over the rest of the season and securing the sixth and final playoff spot. However, they were swept 3-0 by [[Phoenix1]] in the [[NA LCS/2017 Season/Spring Playoffs|playoff quarterfinals]].

Xpecial remained on Dignitas's roster for the [[NA_LCS/2017_Season/Summer_Season|summer split]], but with the acquisition of [[Big]], didn't appear in a game. Before the start of Week 3, he left Dignitas and joined the struggling Phoenix1, who had yet to win a game in the summer split. Xpecial started all of their remaining games and helped them break their loss streak in Week 4, but the team still struggled, finishing in last place with a 4-14 record. This forced them to play in the promotion tournament, where they outlasted challenger team [[Gold Coin United]] in the first round 3-2 but fell to [[Team Liquid]] 3-2 in round 2, before sweeping [[EUnited]] in the final qualification match to requalify for the LCS. Xpecial unexpectedly broke down in tears during a post-game interview with [[Ovilee May]], distraught over his new team being split up. 

===2018 Season===
Phoenix1 was not accepted into the newly franchised LCS for 2020, and Xpecial left the team in November. He eventually joined the newly formed [[Golden Guardians Academy]] for the [[NA_Academy_League/2018_Season/Spring_Season|spring academy split]]. However, the good moments were few on Xpecial's new team, as Golden Guardians Academy spent nearly all of the split in last place and finished with a 2-16 record. For the [[NA_LCS/2018_Season/Summer_Season|summer split]], Xpecial joined the [[Golden Guardians|main roster]] as an assistant coach and coached the team on stage for Week 8 after the departure of [[Tyler]]. Despite his efforts, Golden Guardians finished tenth for the second straight split, and Xpecial left the team immediately after the season ended.  

== Trivia ==
* He was originally the mid laner for Defy All Odds<ref>[http://www.nationalesl.com/us/lol/5on5/emsfinals1/team/log/5645241/ Defy All Odds Team History] ''nationalesl.com''</ref> before joining [[Team SoloMid]] as their replacement for [[FeedFest]].
* Was for a while the quietest member of [[Team SoloMid]]. [[TheOddOne]] and [[Chaox]] repeatedly referred to Xpecial as "Hamster."
* Despite filling his team's role as Support, he is a very skilled Solo Queue AP player, and has even outlaned [[Reginald]] on several occasions.
* Can box better than former AD carry [[Chaox]]. <ref>[http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7nhBd5tJu3A AD carry VS support round 2] "youtube.com"</ref>
* Played three toplane practice games against [[Dyrus]] at [[IGN Proleague Season 4 - Las Vegas]] and won all of them.
* His parents own a vegetarian restaurant.
* Speaks Cantonese, Mandarin, and English.
* Played AP {{ci|Tristana}} a lot while moving up through the solo queue ladder.
* His rune pages on his North American account "Xpecial" are all named after Taylor Swift songs.
* Was for a time considered the best Support in North America by then-Counter Logic Gaming's AD Carry Doublelift.
* One of five players to have qualified for all of the first three World Championships, along with [[Dyrus]], [[Reginald]], [[TheOddOne]] and, [[YellOwStaR]].
* Was the first player in the LCS to reach 1000 career assists.
* Reached 2000 Assists in the LCS on February 18, 2017
** The 1st player to reach 2000 Assists in the LCS.
** His 2000th assist was for [[Dignitas]]'s Jungler [[Chaser]]'s kill on [[Flyquest]]'s Support [[LemonNation]] in the [[NA LCS 2017 Spring|NA LCS 2017 Spring Season]] with {{ci|Zyra}}.
